item.title: Defender XDR documents a Teams synthetic-media hunting table — 13 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 November 2026

Defender XDR documents a Teams synthetic-media hunting table

The period's strongest addition is documentation for the SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents advanced-hunting table, covering Microsoft Teams synthetic-media detections and investigation fields. Endpoint's AI Agent Runtime Protection guidance is more operationally specific: it separates agent-native and network inspection, defines support-matrix requirements, and maps both settings to 0 (Disabled), 1 (Block), and 2 (Audit). Identity migration wording also removes a domain-controller-only limitation statement, while threat-actor naming entries were revised.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents documents Teams deepfake investigation fields

The new Defender XDR advanced-hunting table covers Microsoft Teams synthetic-media detection events and exposes severity, confidence, maliciousness, source, user, and detection-provider details. Results require Defender for Office 365 and an approved detection engine.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

AI Agent Runtime Protection now specifies numeric policy values

The configuration guidance states that both settings use 0 for Disabled, 1 for Block, and 2 for Audit.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Runtime-protection testing now separates agent-native and network inspection

The demonstration guide now uses a support matrix covering inspection methods, agent modes, and minimum versions. It distinguishes agent-native inspection (AiAgentProtection) from network inspection (AiAgentNetworkInspection), removes Beta Channel update-configuration steps, and adds known-issues guidance.

Defender XDR · General

Threat-actor naming tables revise aliases and affiliations

The table adds or revises aliases, affiliations, origins, and references, including new associations for Citrine Sleet, Midnight Blizzard, and Storm-2603; an entry for Storm-2195; and updated classifications for Storm-1249, Storm-2227, and Storm-3069.

Identity · Identity protection

Sensor V3 migration guidance removes a domain-controller-only statement

Troubleshooting wording now refers to Defender for Endpoint sensor onboarding and removes the statement that in-place migration is supported only for domain controllers. Two ontology links were also updated.

item.title: Defender for Office 365 localizes default Mark and notify emails by Outlook language — 12 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 12 November 2026

Defender for Office 365 localizes default Mark and notify emails by Outlook language

The most consequential update is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice that the default Mark and notify email template will follow users’ Outlook language settings, with global rollout stated to start in June 2026. The six Learn updates otherwise form a terminology and navigation pass: Identity guidance now uses identity security in Microsoft Defender, Cloud Apps guidance uses SaaS security terminology in Microsoft Defender, and affected pages refine portal routes and permissions links.

Defender XDR · General

Default Mark and notify templates will follow Outlook language

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will localize the default “Mark and notify” email template based on each user’s Outlook language settings. The Message Center notice says global rollout starts in June 2026; message classification and custom templates do not change.

Identity · Identity protection

Manage Action Accounts guidance now gives the Defender portal path

The documented navigation path is now Settings > Identities > General > Manage action accounts, with updated formatting for the Create new account button.

Identity · Identity protection

Identity role-group guidance adopts Microsoft Defender terminology

The role-groups page title, description, and introductory guidance now refer to identity security capabilities in Microsoft Defender rather than only Defender for Identity. Two ontology links were also added.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

SaaS admin-access guidance now uses Microsoft Defender terminology

The Configure SaaS security admin access article’s title, description, headings, and introductory text now refer to SaaS security capabilities in Microsoft Defender rather than only Defender for Cloud Apps, including its guidance on Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra administrator roles.

Identity · Identity protection

Identity remediation guidance points to the Defender portal

The Remediation Actions page now states that identity remediation actions are performed in the Defender portal and uses shorter links to required-permissions guidance for Disable, Enable, Revoke session, and Force password change.

View all updates for 12 November 2026 →

item.title: Cloud Apps guidance now lists four admin assignments as unavailable in new configurations — 11 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 11 November 2026

Cloud Apps guidance now lists four admin assignments as unavailable in new configurations

The most consequential update concerns Defender for Cloud Apps: App/instance admin, User group admin, Cloud Discovery global admin, and Cloud Discovery report admin assignments cannot be used in new configurations, while existing configurations remain supported. Other substantive updates document AI-agent runtime protection limitations, a possible repeat-quarantine path in Defender for Office 365, a revised MDASH scan recommendation, and Exchange-dependent SACL guidance.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Four Cloud Apps admin assignments are unavailable for new configurations

The guidance states that App/instance admin, User group admin, Cloud Discovery global admin, and Cloud Discovery report admin assignments cannot be used in new configurations. Existing configurations remain supported.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

AI-agent runtime protection guidance adds Audit and Block-mode limitations

Audit mode may incorrectly report a prompt injection block. In Block mode, Claude Code may continue processing a tool response after a reported block; a post-tool-response block cannot undo actions already completed.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Common Attachments routing can trigger quarantine after message release

Messages quarantined by the Common Attachments Filter may be quarantined again after release because of the return mail-flow path. The updated submission guidance says to submit the initial message version to Microsoft.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

MDASH guidance recommends MAI Cyber Preview for scan configuration

The exposure management guidance now recommends MAI Cyber (Preview) as the scan configuration for MDASH.

Identity · Identity protection

Exchange presence or history defines Configuration partition SACL scope

Configuration partition SACL auditing applies to environments that currently have or previously had Microsoft Exchange. Administrators should use Exchange presence or history when determining whether the configuration applies.

item.title: Multi-recipient Defender for Office 365 policies switch to OR matching when modified — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Multi-recipient Defender for Office 365 policies switch to OR matching when modified

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to change multi-recipient threat-policy inclusion from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR) in December 2026 when an affected policy is modified. That can expand policy scope, while existing policies are not automatically converted. Other substantive guidance covers a 100 MiB limit for portal retrieval of quarantined files, verdict enforcement for certain quarantined mail, preview-scoped Azure security tasks in the Defender portal, and consolidated Sentinel connector-health monitoring. Most remaining updates refine terminology, headings, links, metadata, and navigation across Defender XDR and Identity.

Defender XDR · General

Recipient matching changes from Match all to Match any on policy modification

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is scheduled to interpret multiple specified recipient types with Match any (OR), instead of Match all (AND), when a threat-protection policy is modified in December 2026. Existing policies are not auto-converted, but modifying one can expand its scope.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Endpoint guidance limits portal downloads to cloud-backed files up to 100 MiB

The updated Respond File Alerts guidance says portal downloads use a cloud-backed copy rather than the device’s local quarantine. Cloud backup covers files up to 100 MiB; larger files remain quarantined but cannot be downloaded from the portal. Collect file retrieves the current device path and may fail if quarantine removed the original.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Quarantined malware and high-confidence phishing verdicts cannot be bypassed on release

When MX points to Microsoft 365, the updated guidance says malware and high-confidence phishing messages quarantined under that setup cannot bypass their verdict when released. Administrators must resolve the verdict before release.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Azure Defender portal comparison adds four preview-scoped security tasks

The updated comparison lists Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark, security policies, exemptions, and regulatory compliance assessments as available in preview for Azure environments in the Defender portal.

Sentinel · Developer and API

Sentinel guidance consolidates connector-health checks in Data & connectors

The updated guidance describes the Defender portal’s Data & connectors Overview tab for reviewing connector counts, ingestion volume and growth, errors, table fluctuations, and ingestion latency, with links to connector and table details.

View all updates for 10 November 2026 →

item.title: Unified RBAC guidance now requires both Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online toggles — 9 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 9 November 2026

Unified RBAC guidance now requires both Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online toggles

The supplied period is documentation-led, with the strongest administrator impact concentrated in RBAC prerequisites and Microsoft Sentinel operating procedures. Multiple Office 365 policy articles now state that both the Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online permissions toggles under Email & collaboration must be Active for the documented Unified RBAC scenarios. Sentinel guidance marks direct analytics-rule playbook invocation as deprecated, details unified portal data-management controls, and separates Azure RBAC from Defender unified RBAC for playbooks. The Exposure Management exemptions page is now explicitly labeled preview.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Office 365 policy guidance standardizes a two-toggle Unified RBAC prerequisite

The Connection Filter Policies guidance changes from requiring only the Defender for Office 365 toggle to requiring both the Defender for Office 365 and Exchange Online permissions toggles under Email & collaboration to be Active. The same prerequisite now appears across the supplied anti-spam, anti-malware, anti-phishing, outbound spam, quarantine, Safe Attachments, and Safe Links guidance.

Sentinel · Incidents and response

Sentinel marks direct analytics-rule playbook invocation as deprecated

Alert-trigger playbooks and their Microsoft Sentinel Alert triggers remain supported, but direct invocation from analytics rules is deprecated. The revised procedure uses automation rules for alerts generated by one or multiple analytics rules.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel documents unified portal tabs for data and retention management

The guidance now covers connector and table management, transformations, and ingestion-health monitoring in the unified Defender portal through Overview, Connectors, and Tables tabs. It also specifies URBAC Data (manage) and equivalent workspace permissions, limits the experience to commercial cloud, and identifies table-management limitations.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel playbook guidance separates Defender and Azure permission models

The article distinguishes Microsoft Defender SOC Logic Apps and generated playbooks from Sentinel connector Logic Apps. Logic App playbooks require appropriate Azure roles, while generated playbooks require Defender unified RBAC permissions and no Azure roles; investigation-page access is also documented.

Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure

Exposure Management exemptions guidance now carries explicit preview labeling

The Manage exemptions page title and heading now include “(preview),” making the preview designation explicit in the documented capability. Its custom metadata was also changed and an embedded screenshot was removed.

View all updates for 9 November 2026 →

item.title: Defender regional coverage revisions and Threat Analytics PDF exports sharpen admin guidance — 8 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 8 November 2026

Defender regional coverage revisions and Threat Analytics PDF exports sharpen admin guidance

Three Microsoft Learn updates affect two Defender areas. Defender for Cloud’s Data Security Posture Prepare page updates AWS S3 and GCP supported-region lists and adds explicit unsupported-region lists. Its Regional Availability page also revises Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud availability lists and renames sensitivity scan sections to sensitive data discovery. Defender XDR’s Threat Analytics guidance now describes exporting reports from the Microsoft Defender portal to PDF, including threat context, analyst analysis, images, hyperlinks, and related intelligence when available.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Data Security Posture Prepare adds explicit unsupported AWS S3 and GCP region lists

The page updates supported-region lists for AWS S3 and GCP and adds explicit lists of unsupported AWS S3 and GCP regions. Administrators should use the revised coverage when assessing resource support; no action is required by this change alone.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Regional Availability renames sensitive-data sections and revises cloud region lists

The page renames sensitivity scan sections to sensitive data discovery and revises supported and unsupported region lists for Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud scenarios. Use the revised lists when assessing where sensitive data discovery is available.

Defender XDR · General

Threat Analytics guidance details Microsoft Defender portal PDF report export

The documentation now describes exporting reports to PDF, including threat context, analyst analysis, images, hyperlinks, and related intelligence when available. Administrators can save reports for offline review and sharing.

View all updates for 8 November 2026 →

item.title: Full-management transfer guidance arrives as Defender Endpoint iOS 1.1.82260102 improves slow-network reliability — 6 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 November 2026

Full-management transfer guidance arrives as Defender Endpoint iOS 1.1.82260102 improves slow-network reliability

The period brought two substantive administrator updates: new Defender for Cloud guidance for moving Azure subscriptions or management groups into full Defender portal management, and updated Endpoint release information for an iOS build released November 3, 2026.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for Cloud documents Azure moves into full portal management

New guidance covers transferring subscriptions or management groups from Azure portal management to full Defender portal management. It describes transition stages, prerequisites, and post-transfer behavior. Before confirming a move, administrators should account for the one-way transfer, DWU billing, and loss of existing resource-level plan configurations.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Endpoint release notes identify iOS version 1.1.82260102

The updated release information records iOS platform version 1.1.82260102, released November 3, 2026. The build improves redirected-network reliability on slow or low-bandwidth networks and updates translations for advanced diagnostic settings.

item.title: Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 adds Move to Quarantine in late November — 5 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 5 November 2026

Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 adds Move to Quarantine in late November

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is scheduled to gain a remediation action that moves suspicious messages from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine. Defender for Cloud guidance also tightens the operational picture for Arc-enabled SQL Server: proxy support, extension versioning, manual updates, and resource exclusion procedures are now documented. Endpoint changes mainly improve Linux investigation guidance.

Defender XDR · Email and collaboration

Move to Quarantine is coming to Defender for Office 365 Plan 2

A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says Plan 2 will add a remediation action that moves suspicious email from user mailboxes into Defender quarantine. Rollout begins in late November 2026; no action is required, but policy and role reviews are recommended.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Arc proxy SQL support is documented for Defender for SQL extension 2.0.3585.403

Defender for Cloud release notes state that Azure Arc SQL Server instances with Arc proxy enabled are supported with Defender for SQL extension version 2.0.3585.403. The version is available for manual update, automatic rollout has not started, and Arc proxy can route outbound communication for organizations without direct internet access.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for SQL gets documented manual update workflows across Azure management interfaces

A new procedure page covers updating the Defender for SQL extension on Azure Arc-enabled servers and Azure VMs through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, scripts, or REST APIs. It also documents prerequisites, version verification, and the extensions in scope, excluding the SQL IaaS extension and Azure Connected Machine agent from this update workflow.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

SQL exclusion guidance separates Arc servers from Azure VMs

The updated guidance provides separate procedures for Arc-enabled servers and Azure VMs, including Arc extension block or allow lists and an Azure Policy deny assignment. It states that these controls do not uninstall existing extensions or change subscription-level Defender settings; administrators excluding a resource should configure the applicable restriction before uninstalling the extension.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Linux investigation packages now include Defender for Endpoint Client Analyzer data

Updated Endpoint guidance says Linux investigation packages include Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Client Analyzer diagnostics alongside system information, covering installation, configuration, service health, logs, and connectivity.

View all updates for 5 November 2026 →

item.title: GCC AI-agent scope and incident similarity sharpen Defender admin guidance — 4 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 4 November 2026

GCC AI-agent scope and incident similarity sharpen Defender admin guidance

This was a guidance-heavy period rather than a broad rollout: Defender XDR updates spell out GCC AI-agent coverage and add investigation context around similar cases, similar incidents, and recommended correlations. Office 365 Attack Simulation Training guidance now sets expectations for delayed training assignments and follow-up email, while Endpoint release notes identify macOS 101.26092.0012 and its documented fixes. A Sentinel MCP server entry only revises wording for the run hunting query tool, with no administrator action indicated.

Defender XDR · General

GCC support boundaries are explicit for AI agent inventory

The Defender XDR AI Agent Inventory article now says GCC supports agent discovery and inventory, but not agent risk assessment, security recommendations, or the attack surface graph. GCC administrators can use this scope to determine which AI-agent security capabilities are available.

Defender XDR · Incidents and response

Similar cases guidance adds shared-alert and entity context

Investigate Incident Cases now documents opening the Similar cases page, reviewing similarity reasons, and viewing shared alerts and entities. Investigators can use that context to compare handling and identify recurring patterns.

Defender XDR · General

Recommended correlations broaden the attack view without merging incidents

The Recommended correlations filter includes incidents that are not correlated into the current incident, while a Summary-tab card explains potential attack relationships. Related incidents retain their own ownership, status, and lifecycle until merged.

Office 365 · Email and collaboration

Attack Simulation Training guidance flags delays after interactions

The simulations guidance says new training assignments and the follow-up notification email may take time to appear after a simulation interaction. It links to end-user notification details and suggests adding a custom landing-page message about the delay.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

macOS 101.26092.0012 release notes document package-scanning improvements

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint release notes list macOS version 101.26092.0012 with its release, engine, and signature versions, plus bug and performance fixes and optimized memory usage during package scanning. No administrator action is stated.

View all updates for 4 November 2026 →

item.description:

Microsoft will retire the Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs by February 1, 2027; workflows must be manually migrated to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31. Advanced Hunting APIs retire on February 1, 2027

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

AKS Deny policies can block Security Gating provisioning

item.title: Defender portal preview brings Azure plan management, DWU billing, and server onboarding — 20 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 20 October 2026

Defender portal preview brings Azure plan management, DWU billing, and server onboarding

Defender for Cloud is the clear center of gravity: new and revised guidance describes a preview for connecting Azure commercial subscriptions or management groups, managing cloud security plans in the Defender portal, and estimating costs with Defender Workload Units (DWUs). Migration changes configuration scope, makes migrated Azure portal settings view-only, and does not preserve resource-level configurations. Supporting updates clarify tenant-wide server onboarding, broaden Defender for Identity sensor v3.x coverage, and flag an upcoming Defender for Cloud Apps permission change.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Defender for Cloud plan management moves into a scoped portal preview

New preview guidance covers connecting Azure subscriptions or management groups and configuring plans globally or at tenant, management-group, or subscription scope. After migration, plan settings become view-only in the Azure portal, and resource-level configurations are not preserved.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

DWU guidance adds cost estimation and post-adoption reporting

New guidance introduces Defender Workload Units, a Cloud Security Cost Estimator, and a Cloud security cost report. It also documents updated workload measurements, plan consolidations, and DNS billing treatment under the new model.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Direct onboarding is explicitly tenant-wide for eligible non-Azure servers

The updated procedure states that Direct onboarding affects all eligible existing and future non-Azure servers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant; individual-server or pilot-group selection is unsupported. Administrators must verify healthy Defender for Endpoint telemetry, a matching tenant, and the required roles before enabling it.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Defender for Identity sensor v3.x expands to more Windows Server roles

Updated guidance documents sensor v3.x onboarding with or without Defender for Endpoint for eligible Windows Server 2019 or later AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, extending the documented coverage beyond domain controllers.

Defender XDR · General

App Governance permissions will change for three Entra roles

Starting in mid-November 2026, Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will align App Governance role-based access with Defender XDR. The change affects the Cloud App Security, Compliance Administrator, and Compliance Data Administrator roles, so administrators should review and update role assignments.

item.description:
Day in brief · 14 October 2026

Defender for Identity sensor v3 guidance shifts to September cumulative updates

This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day—22 updates and one removed page, with no new entries—but several changes have direct operational consequences. Defender for Identity guidance now centers on September 2026 Windows Server updates and clarifies sensor migration and offboarding behavior. Defender for Cloud documents an AWS scan-suspension threshold, while Defender XDR clarifies both the AIAgentsInfo-to-AgentsInfo schema transition and where DLP signals can be investigated.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Defender for Identity sensor v3 prerequisites move to September 2026 cumulative updates

The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance replaces the July 2026 prerequisite with the September 2026 Windows Server cumulative update for sensor version 3.0.10 or later. It also clarifies that administrators should select the local system account option before v2 migration and that migration does not automatically remove workspace DSA or gMSA configuration.

Identity · Identity protection

Defender for Identity guidance separates Endpoint offboarding from identity-only operation

The FAQ states that offboarding a server from Defender for Endpoint stops Defender for Identity v3.x sensor reporting, including sensors migrated from v2.x, and does not automatically enable identity-only mode. Deployments needing identity-only protection should use the onboarding method that excludes Defender for Endpoint.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

AWS agentless scanning suspends new scans after 250 failed-deletion snapshots

Defender for Cloud guidance says that 250 or more Defender-tagged snapshots accumulated because of deletion authorization failures suspend new scans for the affected AWS scope. The snapshots continue accruing storage charges until deleted, so administrators should verify ec2:DeleteSnapshot authorization and review AWS policy restrictions.

item.description:

AI agent support matrix clarifies Defender for Endpoint’s activity-based discovery

The period’s most consequential administrator guidance concerns local AI agents in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. A new support matrix covers supported agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection by operating system and configuration, while related pages clarify that discovery depends on observed activity. Sentinel also added specific custom-parser guidance. Most remaining updates—32 in Microsoft Security Exposure Management—were page-attribution maintenance.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

New matrix separates AI agent support by operating system and configuration

A new Microsoft Defender for Endpoint article documents supported local AI agents, MCP server discovery, and runtime protection scenarios, with support listed separately by operating system and configuration. It also explains that discovery depends on observed agent activity.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Installed agents may remain absent until Defender observes activity

The local-agent guidance states that Defender lists an agent after observing activity on an onboarded device; installation alone does not guarantee discovery. It also says the inventory is not a complete software inventory, directing administrators to Software inventory for installed-software details and the support matrix for coverage.

item.description:

This documentation-heavy period’s most consequential updates describe a combined Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers experience in the Microsoft Defender portal, clarify when disabling Defender for Servers automatically offboards eligible servers, and replace manual support-log analyzer steps with self-contained Live Response workflows. Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Unified server experience guidance consolidates endpoint and server workflows

The Endpoint page now describes bringing Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Servers together in the Microsoft Defender portal for Azure and on-premises servers, covering server asset views, investigations, hunting, RBAC, and device groups. It states that existing Defender for Endpoint servers require no onboarding, reinstallation, or migration; administrators should still review capability requirements before changing configuration.

Defender for Cloud · Architecture and deployment

Offboarding guidance distinguishes disabling Defender for Servers from a Plan 2-to-Plan 1 switch

The Defender for Cloud tutorial states that disabling Defender for Servers for Azure subscriptions in public preview automatically offboards eligible servers, while switching from Plan 2 to Plan 1 does not trigger automatic offboarding. The updated Endpoint procedure replaces manual analyzer-download steps with self-contained binary or Python Live Response action pairs, adds package validation and workspace-ID handoff, and specifies prerequisites and HTTPS requirements. item.description:

Identity · Identity protection

Identity activation is limited to new sensor v3.x deployments

The updated guidance covers sensor v3.x activation without Defender for Endpoint on eligible Windows Server 2019 or later domain controllers. The deployment article now directs administrators to embed the tenant-specific onboarding file in the golden image, keep `mdatp` stopped during image creation, and start Defender on clones only after each final hostname is set. item.description:

Custom detections spell out 5-minute-to-14-day scheduling and lookback boundaries

The period focuses on guidance changes that sharpen administrator decisions. Custom-detection pages spell out the 5-minute-to-14-day custom-frequency range, the Sentinel-only data-source boundary, fixed 4-hour-to-30-day lookbacks for Defender XDR data, and Sentinel lookback limits that remain in public preview. Other meaningful updates clarify Unified RBAC coverage for identity exclusions, restrict two Cloud Apps admin roles in new configurations, and record four GA Defender for Cloud sensor builds with security and dependency fixes.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

Custom frequency is restricted to Sentinel-only detections

Updated Custom Detection Rules guidance says custom frequency from 5 minutes to 14 days is available only for rules based exclusively on Microsoft Sentinel data. Rules using Defender XDR data instead use fixed lookback periods tied to run frequency, ranging from 4 hours to 30 days, and cannot use custom scoping with this frequency option.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel guidance sets preview lookback ceilings by frequency

item.description:

Sensor 3.0.8 and later requires a July 2026-or-later Windows Server update

The Deploy Sensor V3 guidance requires a July 2026 or later Windows Server cumulative update before installing or upgrading to sensor version 3.0.8 or later for automatic RPC auditing on domain controllers. The troubleshooting guidance states that migration fails when the Defender for Identity workspace and Defender for Endpoint onboarding for the same server belong to different Microsoft tenants. The server may appear ready, but sensor v3.x activation fails.

item.description:
Day in brief · 8 September 2026

Sentinel parser guidance forbids cross-table enrichment and preserves one output per source record

The day’s most consequential updates sharpen Sentinel parser guidance and revise the documented severity of seven Azure Storage alerts to Informational. Defender XDR added dedicated guidance for mapping Advanced Hunting results into graphs, while Defender for Identity added resolution steps for the Sensor v3.x RPC Audit Misconfigured health alert. The remaining edits are primarily layout, link, terminology, and explanatory maintenance.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel parser guidance sets strict source and cardinality boundaries

The updated normalization guidance limits parsers to the declared source table, requires one normalized output per source record, and permits scalar or local static mappings. It explicitly prohibits cross-table enrichment, watchlists, multi-value expansion, joins, aggregation, and deduplication. Source filtering must use fields in the current event; missing source information should be handled in the connector or source-specific table.

Sentinel · Cloud and workloads

Sentinel parser-creation guidance permits lookup mappings only with unique keys

The parser-creation skills guidance says each source record is normalized independently and record cardinality is preserved. Query-local datatable or lookup mappings are allowed when lookup keys are unique, while same-table and cross-table event enrichment are not used.

Defender XDR · Hunting and detection

New Defender XDR guidance details graph mapping for Advanced Hunting

The new guide explains how to prepare query results, configure graph nodes and edges, apply relationship conditions, and use recognized entity types and identifiers for Defender enrichment.

Defender for Cloud · Cloud and workloads

Seven documented Azure Storage alert entries now list their severity as Informational instead of High, Medium, or Low variants. Administrators reviewing the alert reference should use the revised labels when prioritizing those entries.

item.title: Sentinel table migration and Linux enforcement changes sharpen administrator action — 4 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 4 September 2026

Sentinel table migration and Linux enforcement changes sharpen administrator action

The period was dominated by documentation maintenance, but several updates carry direct operational weight. Sentinel guidance now points administrators from the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table to ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects, while Defender for Endpoint documents four Linux antivirus enforcement levels, a passive default, and Preview audit mode. Other consequential changes include SIEM-agent deprecation guidance for the Cloud Apps integration, manual Preview activation limits for Defender for Identity v3.x sensors on non-domain controllers, and material changes to the documented Defender XDR DataSecurityEvents schema.

Sentinel · Hunting and detection

Sentinel threat-intelligence content must move off the legacy table

The STIX guidance directs content to the ThreatIntelIndicators and ThreatIntelObjects schemas and states that ingestion into the legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table stops after July 31, 2025. Custom queries, analytics and detection rules, workbooks, and automation using the old table should be updated.

Endpoint · Endpoint protection

Linux antivirus enforcement now has four documented levels

The Linux configuration article lists four antivirus enforcement levels, identifies passive as the default, and marks audit mode as Preview. It adds verification guidance for the active level; audit mode requires Defender for Endpoint version 101.26062.0007 or later.

Cloud Apps · Cloud and workloads

Cloud Apps integration guidance now deprecates SIEM agents

The Sentinel integration page states that SIEM agents are deprecated while the Microsoft Sentinel integration (Preview) remains supported, and adds a dedicated integration section. Organizations still using SIEM agents should review their integration strategy against the supported Sentinel option.

Identity · Architecture and deployment

Defender for Identity documents manual v3.x activation on additional servers

The v3.x sensor deployment guidance now covers non-domain-controller AD FS, AD CS, and Microsoft Entra Connect servers. Activation on those servers is in Preview and requires manual activation; automatic activation and migration are unsupported. Deployments limited to these servers should include at least one v3.x sensor on a domain controller.

Defender XDR · General

DataSecurityEvents reference adds and removes hunting columns

The Defender XDR table reference removes its Preview and prerelease notices, adds physical access, removable media, and risky AI usage fields, and removes several URL, email, file-path, workload, and Cloud App Alert fields. Query and integration owners should review dependencies on the removed columns.

item.description:
Day in brief · 2 September 2026

Defender for Office 365 will quarantine AI-targeting prompt injections by default

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is preparing prompt injection protection for email, with rollout scheduled from July through October 2026 for organizations with Defender Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5. The remaining updates are targeted guidance and documentation corrections: Defender XDR now specifies required device identifiers for Sentinel-mapped activity, Defender for Identity documents custom service-account classification, and Endpoint troubleshooting corrects a registry-path typo.

Defender XDR · Email and collaboration

Prompt injection protection planned for email

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will detect and quarantine malicious email content targeting AI assistants. For organizations with Defender Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5, automatic high-confidence threat quarantine is enabled by default during the July–October 2026 rollout, with no required administrator action.

Defender XDR · General

Device Timeline mappings require specific identifiers

The Entity Page guidance now specifies that custom activity data mapped from Sentinel to Microsoft Defender XDR must include either HostName plus NTDomain or HostName plus DnsDomain for correct Device Timeline visibility.

Identity · Identity protection

Custom rules can identify missed service accounts

Defender for Identity guidance explains that custom classification rules can identify service accounts not detected automatically, including accounts using an `srv` prefix.

Endpoint · Troubleshooting

Endpoint troubleshooting path corrected

The troubleshooting guidance corrects the `ProductAppDataPath` registry value from `Microsft` to `Microsoft` in the Windows Defender data path, giving administrators the accurate registry path to use when following the procedure.
